summary:
The meeting began with a proposal to restructure the engineering key review into four department-specific sessions operating on a two-month rotation to improve visibility and reduce calendar fatigue. The team agreed to trial this approach while remaining flexible to adjust frequency based on department size and needs. Following this, the discussion shifted to refining engineering KPIs, specifically addressing the complexity of tracking community contributions versus internal merge requests.

A significant portion of the review focused on data infrastructure and defect tracking metrics. The team addressed a Postgres replication lag issue, agreeing that Infrastructure should lead on provisioning a dedicated host for data engineering workloads while exploring database tuning options. Additionally, feedback was provided to overhaul how defect SLOs are measured, moving away from tracking closed bugs toward monitoring the percentage of open bugs that remain within or exceed SLO timeframes to prevent metric gaming.

The session concluded with updates on System Usability Scale (SUS) scores, which showed a stabilizing trend despite recent declines, and a review of the narrow MR rate. Context was provided regarding seasonal dips and vacation days, leading to a strategic decision to cap the MR rate target at 10. Going forward, the engineering team will maintain this productivity baseline while shifting focus toward improving quality, security, and availability metrics.

key_points.text: Proposal to split the engineering key review into a two-month rotating schedule for Development/Quality and Security/UX departments.
Decision to simplify community contribution tracking by measuring the percentage of total MRs from the community instead of complex wider/narrow rates.
Identification of Postgres replication lag requiring a dedicated host for data engineering and potential database tuning.
Shift in defect tracking methodology to measure the percentage of open bugs within SLO timeframes rather than focusing on closed bugs.
Narrow MR rate target will be held at 10, with strategic focus shifting to quality, security, and availability improvements.

chapters.title: Narrow MR Rate Context & Target Review

decisions: Adopt a two-month rotating schedule for department key reviews (Development/Quality in month one, Security/UX in month two).
Replace the R&D wider MR rate KPI with a simpler metric tracking the percentage of total MRs originating from the community.
Shift defect SLO measurement from closed bugs to the percentage of open bugs remaining within or exceeding SLO timeframes.
Cap the narrow MR rate target at 10 and redirect engineering focus toward quality, security, and availability metrics.

action_items.text: Work with Mac to transition the KPI dashboard to track the percentage of total MRs from the community.
Add an update on the Postgres replication lag issue and dedicated host plan to next week's InfraKey review.
Investigate the S2 mean time to close spike and provide a deeper analysis at the next meeting.
Develop and deliver the new chart measuring the percentage of open bugs within/outside SLO in the data metrics work stream.
